parsed.explanation: The combined national-state regime creates documented traveller-facing exposures: passport/visa sex-marker mismatch can trigger refusal, secondary inspection, passport confiscation, or possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; national rules restrict gender-congruent access to government-funded facilities; the state facility law covers airports and government buildings and can produce criminal trespass after refusal, with one dismissed arrest; national immigration and corrections custody show severe documented abuse. Protections are partial: existing X passports remain valid until expiry, litigation and legal-aid guidance exist, national hate-crime and employment protections apply, private businesses are outside the state facility law, and trespass is not automatic. Facility exclusion is nonetheless universal in covered spaces and recourse is not shown to remedy it. Street-violence data is concerning but lacks a background denominator. An adult travelling with a trans minor faces added care and guardian/school threats.

entry_documents.exposure: Parent passport/visa rules require M/F assigned sex; X not issued; discrepancy can lead to refusal, secondary inspection, passport confiscation, possible lifetime fraud finding; trans athlete entry ban.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; fraud finding not automatic; litigation and legal-aid FAQ; limited waiver possibilities.
entry_documents.interaction: Border/visa check can escalate to investigation, detention or removal; state document rules cannot fix a foreign passport.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National immigration custody documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of trans men; corrections conversion practices, hormone removal and care denial; reporting stopped.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime law and court injunctions not shown to protect custody; consular access not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Passport discrepancy can lead to secondary inspection, refusal, immigration detention and birth-sex custody exposure; state jails are covered by the facility law.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars gender-congruent access to government-funded single-sex facilities; state law bars restrooms/changing in state/local government buildings including airports, schools, prisons and detention; criminal trespass after refusal; one arrest.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Private businesses outside state law; trespass requires willful entry plus refusal; sole prosecution dismissed on standing; no later arrest documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State facility ban operates on top of national facility restriction; an airport encounter can move into state criminal process.

care_services.exposure: State restricts adult care with waiting periods, insurance bars and physician-only rules, bans minor care, and allows conscience refusal; national insurance bar proposed; care records subpoenaed.
care_services.protection: Some care bans enjoined or blocked; national employment and hate-crime protections do not cover care; no visitor emergency-care protocol documented.
care_services.interaction: A traveller needing HRT or emergency care may face refusal, documentation outing, or pharmacy/insurance mismatch; minor care especially restricted.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National executive orders, justice-department guidance and counterterrorism language frame 'gender ideology' and 'radically pro-transgender' groups as threats; school prosecution threats; state bathroom enforcement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 2020 employment ruling; some court injunctions; local protections covering about 55% of population.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile framing raises police/reporting risk and chills recourse; national protections coexist with enforcement of border and facility restrictions.

minors_guardians.exposure: National order threatens prosecution of teachers using preferred names/pronouns; minor care banned in this state; custody laws target gender-affirming care; trans children detained at protests.
minors_guardians.protection: Some care provisions enjoined; no documented visitor-minor safeguard; marriage equality irrelevant to these exposures.
minors_guardians.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor faces care denial, school/guardian threat and document mismatch alongside border and facility exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State reported 3.7 trans women murdered per 100k/year and labelled Do Not Travel; state hate-crime law omits gender identity; police enforce bathroom restrictions.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; state human-relations commission enforces national employment holding; local ordinances cover about 55% of population.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to anti-trans violence is uneven; a victim may avoid reporting due to official hostility or facility enforcement.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport policy, care rules, bathroom statute and state document rules remain unresolved in litigation; travel advisories are dated; airport application and fraud-finding practice undocumented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Litigation ongoing; legal-aid FAQ; one bathroom prosecution dismissed; private businesses outside state facility law.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists but is not shown to change border or facility outcomes; unresolved rules create planning and escalation risk.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.25-A describes ad hoc detention, humiliation and cash extortion with uncertain registry logging. This dossier is more legally structured but adds codified facility exclusion, national border fraud exposure and documented custody abuse; it lacks a documented shakedown pattern. Net roughly similar, slightly below 0.25.

0.35-A has no imprisonment threat and ends in administrative denial and exclusion. Here covered government facilities including airports carry criminal trespass after refusal, national facilities are restricted, and detention custody is documented abusive. Materially below 0.35.

0.55-B shows a working charter intervention that permits onward travel after delay. Here protections are partial or untested, while border/document and facility rules continue to operate. Much below 0.55.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines national border/document screening with state facility exclusion. A trans visitor with a marker mismatch can be refused entry or investigated; using a congruent restroom in covered government buildings, including airports, risks an order to leave and a trespass charge if refused. National custody is documented abusive, making any detention severe. Private hotels and businesses are outside the state facility statute, national hate-crime and employment protections exist, existing X passports remain valid, and the sole bathroom prosecution was dismissed; these mitigate but do not remedy universal facility exclusion or border fraud exposure. Street-violence data lacks a background denominator. A minor accompanying an adult faces added care and guardian/school threats.
